Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

ggvfields 1.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-11-15

Changes in behavior

  • Streams are now computed with a Runge-Kutta 4 integrator by default (method = "rk4"), in geom_stream_field() and its relatives as well as geom_gradient_field(type = "stream"), geom_stream_smooth() and geom_gradient_smooth(). Streams follow the field more closely, which changes avg_spd slightly. Streams stop at sinks and at singularities such as point charges, and cross jumps in the field, such as one defined with sign() or ifelse(). The adaptive deSolve integrator remains available as method = "lsoda", and "euler" is also available. An unknown method is an error.
  • geom_stream_field2() and stat_stream_field2() now grow every stream to length L and then crop all of them back to the time of the fastest one, so a stream’s length shows its speed relative to the fastest, as the vectors of geom_vector_field2() do. type = "vector" is unchanged.
  • Mapped lengths are proportional to the mapped value: in geom_vector2(), geom_vector_field2() and geom_gradient_field2(type = "vector"), a vector with half the largest norm is drawn half as long. The longest vector is max_range centimeters (0.5 by default; set it with scale_length_continuous()), and the legend shows the same lengths.
  • The ellipses and wedges of geom_vector_smooth(method = "gam"), the default, are now prediction intervals for a new observation at each location, as for method = "lm" and method = "kriging": they include each component’s residual variance as well as the variance of the fit. They are larger than before.
  • The wedges of geom_vector_smooth(pi_type = "wedge") are computed from the exact distribution of the angle of the predicted vector tip, so they cover the stated conf_level however large the uncertainty, and are asymmetric when the uncertainty is. They are wider than before where the uncertainty is large.
  • Supplying formula with the default method = "gam" in geom_stream_smooth(), stat_stream_smooth(), geom_vector_smooth() or stat_vector_smooth() now gives a warning, since the gam smoothers fit fx and fy with s(x, y). Use method = "lm" to fit a formula.
  • The default of conf_level in geom_vector_smooth() is now 0.95. Results are the same.

New features and improvements

  • geom_stream_smooth(), geom_vector_smooth() and their stats work with small data sets: with fewer than 30 distinct locations the gam smoother uses half as many basis functions as locations. At least 5 locations are needed; with fewer, the error suggests method = "lm".
  • With a supplied grid data frame, the default length L of vectors and streams is 0.85 times the grid’s spacing (the median distance between neighboring points), so dense grids do not overplot. Regular grids get the same length as before.
  • geom_vector_smooth() and stat_vector_smooth() choose the interval style by default (pi_type = NULL): ellipses at eval_points and wedges on a grid, without a message. They also gain xlim and ylim to set the range of the grid, which defaults to the range of the data.
  • geom_vector_smooth(method = "kriging") estimates the range of its variogram from the data and works in standardized coordinates, so the smoothed field does not depend on the units of x and y. The fitted coregionalization is kept positive definite.
  • Vectors in polar form take their magnitude from the norm aesthetic, the same name as the computed variable, with angle or angle_deg. distance is accepted as another name for it. The stream smoothers take polar input without an “unknown aesthetics” warning.
  • geom_gradient_field(), geom_gradient_field2() and their stats take a method argument for the stream integrator, as geom_stream_field() does.
  • stat_vector_smooth() is exported.
  • StatStreamSmooth and StatGradientSmooth are the stats behind geom_stream_smooth() and geom_gradient_smooth().
  • stat_vector() maps color = after_stat(norm) by default, like geom_vector().
  • geom_gradient_field2(type = "vector") and stat_gradient_field2(type = "vector") map length = after_stat(norm), so vectors are scaled by the size of the gradient, like geom_vector_field2(). Streams are unchanged.
  • Layers computed from a function (stat_stream_field(), geom_gradient_field(), geom_gradient_field2(), geom_potential() and their stat_*() versions) default to inherit.aes = FALSE, like geom_vector_field() and geom_stream_field(), so they can be added to a plot that has its own data, for example to draw a field behind observed vectors.
  • stat_stream_field() passes normalize and stat_stream_field2() passes tol through to the computation, as geom_stream_field() and geom_stream_field2() do.
  • efield_maker() passes k and q_test to the field it returns, and the field keeps the argument values efield_maker() was called with, so fields can be made in a loop.
  • linetype applies to vector layers such as geom_vector() and geom_vector_field().

Stream speeds (avg_spd)

  • avg_spd, the default color of streams, is the length of the drawn stream divided by the time it took, in every mode:
    • streams run to a time T, and streams with normalize = FALSE that are cropped to the time of the fastest stream, use that shared time, so color and length agree;
    • a stream run to a length L that stops short of it at a sink would take unbounded time to reach the sink, so its speed is measured up to 99% of the length it achieved. This makes it the same for every integrator.

Bug fixes

  • Streams stop where the field becomes infinite, and the field function is only called at finite points.

  • Streams computed with method = "lsoda" only include points where the field is defined, so a stream that runs to the edge of the field’s domain is drawn up to that edge.

  • geom_vector_smooth() takes a fixed or mapped colour for its vectors (blue by default), and keeps a fixed linewidth when there is a single evaluation point.

  • geom_gradient_smooth() keeps a color mapping supplied in mapping, and every field layer, including geom_gradient_field2(), gives the same error for an unknown type.

  • geom_stream_smooth(), geom_gradient_smooth() and geom_vector_smooth() always use the stat that fits their model; a different stat is ignored with a warning.

  • Centered streams (center = TRUE, the default) are drawn when a stream can move only one way from its seed, for example on the edge of the domain where the field is defined.

  • Stream layers skip seed points where the field is undefined, for example a grid point on a charge with efield_maker(), and draw the remaining streams.

  • geom_stream() gives the same message as geom_path() when every group has a single observation.

  • geom_stream_smooth() and stat_stream_smooth() accept fixed aesthetics such as color = "red" or linewidth = 2 without a warning, and respect colour = "red".

Performance

  • geom_stream_smooth() and geom_gradient_smooth() fit their model once per group rather than at every evaluation of the field, which is much faster.
  • Computing streams with method = "lsoda" is about twice as fast.

Documentation

  • The help pages document the defaults of pi_type in geom_vector_smooth() (ellipses at eval_points, wedges on a grid) and of n in geom_potential(), whose fun returns a vector.
  • The smoothers are documented as using a gam by default, with formula applying to method = "lm".
  • Angles in geom_stream_smooth() are documented as radians, and the geom_vector_smooth() examples are clarified.
  • The help for geom_stream_field(), geom_vector_field() and geom_gradient_field() describes how L, T and normalize set the length of streams and vectors, including that a centered stream run to a time T runs for T in each direction.
  • geom_gradient_field() documents its default type ("vector") and its default colors (norm for vectors, avg_spd for streams).
  • The norm computed variable, L in geom_vector2(), log in efield() and the computed variables of geom_potential() are described more precisely.
  • Examples are run when the package is checked.
  • The pkgdown site is at https://dustysturner.com/ggvfields/.

Internal

  • sp and gstat are suggested rather than imported, since only method = "kriging" in geom_vector_smooth() needs them; you are asked to install them the first time you use it. farver is no longer a dependency, and rlang is declared.
  • The package uses only exported ggplot2 functions.
  • Each geom_*() / stat_*() pair is built by one shared internal constructor, and a test checks that both members of a pair pass the same parameters and default mappings.
  • Errors are raised with cli throughout.
  • Added tests for the changes above, visual snapshot tests with vdiffr (now in Suggests; CRAN skips them), and an R CMD check workflow.

ggvfields 1.0.1

CRAN release: 2026-06-18

  • Fixed the length legend for geom_vector_field2() (and the related stream geoms): GeomStream now uses a custom draw_key that dispatches to draw_key_length() when the length aesthetic is mapped, so the legend relating segment lengths to vector norms is drawn again.
  • Corrected the handling of the time variable t in geom_stream().
  • Fixed the draw order of grobs in the stream and vector geoms and suppressed spurious output from the kriging step.
  • Fixed handling of the linewidth argument.
  • Added an option to choose between gam and lm when smoothing.

ggvfields 1.0.0

CRAN release: 2025-03-15
